diagnostics.note: Bernoulli-at-row-share: each fixture resampled w.p. its share of all rows -> E[#resampled fixtures] = sum_k (n_k/N_total) = 1.0 of 903 (measured 1.000).  Each replicate pools ~1 resampled fixture (avg ~15-20 rows, mostly a single LEP+topology), so the replicate rate is either 0 (no positive fixture drawn) or a near-single-fixture rate -> the stored [0.0, 0.6111]. This is a RESAMPLING-UNIT DEFECT, not a valid cluster CI. The correct resample-the-fixture bootstrap resamples all 903 fixtures w/r each replicate.

m1.verdict: the stored [0.0, 0.6111] is an IMPLEMENTATION DEFECT (resampling unit: Bernoulli at per-cluster row-share collapses to ~1 resampled fixture/replicate). The correct resample-the-cluster bootstrap is reported above; the wide stored interval is NOT a legitimate statistical consequence and is superseded.

cluster_stats_note: The downstream_results summary.json already carries a cluster-BINOMIAL CI (fraction of clusters containing >=1 positive, e.g. M1 [0.605, 0.6413] over 2729 clusters) — a DIFFERENT, valid cluster-aware estimate.  The stored m1_fixture_cluster_bootstrap95 is the row-level rate over a degenerate resampling; the two are reported separately.
